Learning bank

Research to examine. Works to teach. Claims to test.

A selected starting collection of 53 sources, with particular attention to Levin, Solms and Berg. Recent research sits beside foundational studies and cultural works. Each entry identifies what it can—and cannot—support.

Empirical study2025-04-14

Revealing non-trivial information structures in aneural biological tissues via functional connectivity

Blackiston, Dromiack, Grasso and colleagues, including Michael Levin

Calcium imaging in six frog epidermal organoids reveals structured patterns of functional connectivity before and after injury. Methods used for neural tissue can also investigate non-neural coordination.

Teaching use & evidence notes

Teaching use Read the author summary and inspect Figure 1. Separate a measured signal, an inferred network and a claim about mind.

Limit Functional connectivity is a statistical relationship. Neither network structure nor coordinated repair establishes subjective experience. The sample is small.

Access Open source.

Review depth Abstract and publication record checked. Checked 2026-10-10.

Michael Levin and David B. Resnik

Proposes treating goal-directedness and cognition as testable approaches to interacting with biological systems across scales.

Limit This is a conceptual framework drawing on experiments, not an experiment establishing that all matter has experience.

The Hard Problem of Consciousness and the Free Energy Principle

Develops an account of consciousness centered on affect, bodily needs and uncertainty, connecting neuropsychology with the free energy principle.

Limit A theoretical synthesis. The proposed explanation of subjective experience remains contested; feeling, cognition and cortical processing are not interchangeable terms.

Study A.I. Consciousness? The Bots Would Like a Word With You.

Teaching use Pair with Berg’s self-report preprint. Separate what was observed, who verified it, and how each participant interprets it; trace the role of the human’s instructions in the agent’s behavior.

Limit Reported anecdotes are not controlled evidence of consciousness. The provenance of some emails is uncertain. The absence of a universally accepted consciousness test does not mean that all evidence or competing explanations have equal weight.

Hyecho’s pilgrimage account — translation and teaching context

Hyecho · Translation by Matty Wegehaupt, in the volume translated by Wegehaupt, Michael Finch and Sem Vermeersch; edited by Roderick Whitfield

Hyecho’s account provides a historical source for studying Buddhist pilgrimage and encounters across Asia. The University of Michigan’s Hyecho’s Journey project credits Korean Buddhist Culture: Accounts of a Pilgrimage, Monuments, and Eminent Monks (Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, 2012) for its journal quotations.

Teaching use & evidence notes

Teaching use Develop a historically grounded companion selection on observation, religious practice, translation and the interpretation of another person’s experience. Choose the passage with the translator before adding it to the common syllabus.

Limit The surviving account is fragmentary. Descriptions of places and practices do not give transparent access to the traveler’s inner experience. Michigan’s project credits its poem translations separately to Chun Wa Chan and Kevin Carr.

Access Open project context and selected quotations; consult the 2012 volume for the translation.

The project gives Jikji’s full title, its English rendering as The Essential Passages Pointing Directly to Mind, and its 1377 metal-type and 1378 woodblock editions.

Teaching use & evidence notes

Teaching use Connect the characters 直指心體 to translation, Buddhist practice and the material forms of the book.

Limit The title establishes a direct textual connection to mind; it does not make Buddhist mind equivalent to a modern scientific concept.

Access Open research overview.

Review depth Jikji title and edition descriptions read. Checked 2026-10-10.

Institutional resource2021-06-22

The History of Printing in Asia — Part 1

Ryan Wolfson-Ford, Library of Congress

The Library of Congress places early printing in East Asia and describes Buddhist woodblock texts and Bi Sheng’s eleventh-century earthenware movable type.

Teaching use & evidence notes

Teaching use Place Jikji within an already substantial Asian printing history before comparing it with Gutenberg.

Limit Earlier printing history must be distinguished from the earliest surviving metal-type book. Routes of transmission to Europe remain uncertain.

Access Open institutional article.

Review depth Early printing and movable-type sections read. Checked 2026-10-10.

Cultural workca. 1550–721 BCE

Heart amulet with human head

Ancient Egyptian object; Metropolitan Museum of Art

This funerary amulet combines a stylized stone heart with a small human head. The museum dates it approximately 1550–721 BCE.

Teaching use & evidence notes

Teaching use Compare material representations of the heart with the Greenfield Papyrus source.

Limit Its form alone does not establish a theory of mind. Pair it with textual evidence about heart, mind and memory.

Cultural workModeled ca. 1880; cast ca. 1910

The Thinker

Auguste Rodin; Metropolitan Museum of Art

The sculpture gives thought a bodily form through a seated, concentrated figure. This cast dates to around 1910, from a model conceived around 1880.

Teaching use & evidence notes

Teaching use Compare sculpture with lexical and bodily representations of mental life.

Limit The meaning belongs to a particular artwork and its history, not to every seated posture.

Scope of this edition

Checked 10 October 2026. The collection draws on the Levin Lab publication list, Reciprocal Research’s listed outputs, selected Solms papers, original publication records and institutional cultural resources. It is a selected reading bank, not a systematic review or a complete research inventory.

Publication status and evidence type are separate: a peer-reviewed theoretical paper still presents a theory. An abstract-level check is identified as such. A source’s date does not imply that it is the newest work in its field.

Priority gaps include recent research on music and sport, deeper review of the new multicultural slate, disability and neurodiversity scholarship, animal cognition, and a broader literary selection. Sources need deeper review and teaching trials before final adoption.
